messages:
margot: quick follow-up to the RFC I posted earlier — proposing we make golden-sample rotation pluggable and split the bench-runner from the validator processes. goal: faster iterations on golden sets without touching the validator infra. thoughts?
rajeev: +1 to pluggable rotation. main risk is drift: different rotations across clusters could hide regressions. we need a canonical source-of-truth and an opt-in migration window.
sam: can you sketch the interface? i'd prefer a tiny RPC/manifest format rather than reloading code paths.
margot: sure — rough sketch:
```
rotation manifest v1:
- id: golden-v2
- created_by: telemetry-service
- buckets: [slice-A, slice-B]
- ttl_days: 14
- signature: <sig>
```
benchbot: nightly-smoke: bench_runner failed on quantized-rt: Tokenizer mismatch for model cx-26
benchbot: snippet: `ERROR: tokenizer.vocab_size=50256 != expected=50260`
li: we need a validation step that checks tokenizer fingerprint before running benches — otherwise bench noise.
kevin: splitting runner vs validator sounds good. validator should be stateless and idempotent; runner can be ephemeral and optimizable for throughput.
margot: tradeoffs: 1) pluggable rotation => ops overhead + more moving parts. 2) single canonical manifest reduces drift but adds central write path (telemetry-service?). 3) validator lint step adds ~200ms to onboarding but catches obvious mismatches.
sam: could we make the validator do a quick fingerprint check and short-circuit heavy benches? e.g. if tokenizer fingerprint mismatch -> fail fast and skip full bench.
rajeev: yes — fail-fast lint. then schedule a re-run on staging with converted tokenizer.
maya: question: how do we keep historical golden sets reproducible for audits? if rotation is pluggable we still need immutable archives.
margot: plan: rotation manifests are pointers; each manifest entry must include immutable artifact hashes and an archive pointer (s3://goldens/sha256). rotation + archives versioned.
kevin: rollout plan idea: 1) deploy validator lint in canary, 2) enable manifest read-only for benches, 3) allow rotation writes from telemetry-service with a feature flag, 4) force migration of any mismatched models via opt-out window.
li: metrics: track bench-failure-rates pre/post, golden-drift-alerts, and time-to-fix for tokenizer mismatches. add trace ids to manifests.
sam: small API sketch for validator lint:
```
POST /validator/lint
payload: { model_id, artifacts: [sha], expected_tokenizer_fp }
resp: { ok: bool, reason?: string, fallback_suggestion?: string }
```
margot: owner proposals: margot + li for design, sam for API, rajeev for ops/runbook, kevin for rollout. agree?
maya: agree, will help with audit requirements.
kevin: timeline proposal: 2-week spike to implement manifest format + lint + bench read-only support. aim for canary by EOW + 2.
rajeev: note: we should add a migration helper to re-tokenize corpora if tokenizer changes; otherwise a lot of manual churn.
li: also consider running lightweight synthetic benches early (short sequences) to detect regressions fast.
sam: +1 — synthetic quickcheck before full bench.
margot: awesome. i'll draft the follow-up RFC with above and include a migration checklist and telemetry events. will ping owners shortly. :tada:
kevin: :thumbsup:
benchbot: scheduled run: bench_runner --manifest=s3://goldens/manifest-golden-v2.json --mode=dryrun
margot: next action: margot will open the RFC PR today, sam/lee/rajeev will add API and ops comments. meeting if needed after initial PR review.
